items.title: Storybooks Korea (Global Storybooks)
items.creator: Global African Storybook Project (global-asp)
items.why: 40 short illustrated children's stories in plain 해요체, sorted into levels 1-5; the Level 1 books are one short sentence per page.
items.notes: FETCHABLE STATIC HTML (GitHub Pages). Story text is in <h3> elements, one per page; images are separate files. Enumerate: the home page lists all 40 stories with level; URL pattern /storybooks-korea/stories/ko/NNNN/ (4-digit ID); level index pages /storybooks-korea/stories/ko/level1 ... level5. Counts: L1=15, L2=11, L3=8, L4=4, L5=2. Site levels 1-2 map to our 1-2; site levels 3-5 are still children's stories (our 2-3). Translated African stories, so some names/places are foreign. Text length ranges from ~340 chars (L1) to ~6,000 chars (L5).

items.title: StoryWeaver 한국어 동화
items.creator: Pratham Books
items.why: About 1,000 Korean picture books, each tagged level 1-4; level 1 titles are a few words per page.
items.notes: NOT FETCHABLE AS STATIC HTML: the site is a JavaScript single-page app; a plain fetch of a story or /read page returns only a loading placeholder, and /api/v1/stories/{slug}/read returns 401. Metadata is open: GET https://storyweaver.org.in/api/v1/books-search?languages[]=Korean&per_page=N returns JSON (996 Korean hits on 2026-11-06) with title, slug and level; GET /api/v1/stories/{slug} returns title/authors/level, but no page text. Story page = https://storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/{slug}. It works only if the extension renders the page in a real tab and scrapes the DOM. Example slugs (level): 60168-rabbit-and-turtle 토끼와 거북이 (1), 19547-bbalgan-yeon 빨간 연 (1), 264087-gaemidul 개미들 (1), 60285-a-liar-who-has-become-a-cow 소가 된 거짓말쟁이 (1), 102547-a-gi-won-sung-i-ui-ireobeorin-ba-na-na 아기 원숭이가 잃어버린 바나나 (2), 142851-a-cat-s-daily-life 고양이의 일상 (2), 18804-jogeumssik-jogeumssik 조금씩 조금씩 (2), 156108-dali-sarajin-baam 달이 사라진 밤 (3), 59784-mool-ee-daechae-eodiro-sarajingeollkka 물이 대체 어디로 사라진걸까? (4). Licence: StoryWeaver's open-content page says CC BY 4.0 for all stories and illustrations (check each book; a few are public domain).

items.title: 위키문헌 분류:동화
items.creator: Korean Wikisource (mostly 방정환 texts from 《어린이》, 1922-1929)
items.why: Public-domain 1920s children's stories in modern Hangul with 습니다 narration; short but with some dated words.
items.notes: FETCHABLE HTML. 21 pages on 2026-11-06 (19 main namespace + 2 '번역:' pages). Enumerate with the MediaWiki API: https://ko.wikisource.org/w/api.php?action=query&list=categorymembers&cmtitle=분류:동화&cmlimit=50&format=json (verified). Pages can also be fetched as clean HTML with action=parse. Several items are Bang Jeong-hwan's 1920s adaptations of Western tales (눈의 여왕, 빨간구두, 털보 장사 = The Selfish Giant). Some old words (인제, 그려, 예끼) and occasional hanja glosses; occasional typos (금도끼 has '바렸습니다').

items.why: A classic 전래동화 opening ('옛날 호랑이 담배 먹을 적') in about 2,000 characters, with some dialect and hanja glosses.
items.notes: 《어린이》 New Year issue, 1926.

items.title: 시골쥐 서울 구경
items.creator: 방정환 (Bang Jeong-hwan), 1926
items.why: A familiar town-mouse/country-mouse fable, about 3,000 characters, in mostly modern spelling.
items.notes: 《어린이》 vol. 4 no. 10, October 1926.

items.title: 설떡 술떡
items.titleEn: New Year Rice Cake, Wine Rice Cake
items.creator: 방정환 (Bang Jeong-hwan), 1926
items.why: A short Lunar New Year story (about 1,400 characters) with holiday vocabulary.
items.notes: 《어린이》 vol. 4 no. 1, January 1926. Some hanja glosses such as 설(正初).

items.title: 이상한 샘물
items.creator: 방정환 (Bang Jeong-hwan), 1923
items.why: The classic 'water of youth' folktale opening with 옛날, 어느 산 밑에..., about 4,000 characters.
items.notes: 《어린이》, July 1923.

items.title: 털보 장사
items.creator: Oscar Wilde, tr. 방정환 (Bang Jeong-hwan), 1922
items.why: A story many learners already know in English, in about 8,000-10,000 characters of 습니다 narration.
items.notes: 《개벽》, November 1922. The longest of the set; some 1920s vocabulary (으레히).

items.title: 어린이동아
items.creator: 동아일보 (Dong-A Ilbo)
items.why: Daily news written for primary-school children in 해요체, with hard words explained in brackets (e.g. 야당(정치 권력을 잡고 있지 않은 정당)).
items.notes: FETCHABLE HTML (checked with curl; WebFetch's crawler is blocked by the site). Full article body is in the static HTML, no login (e.g. https://kids.donga.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=170240, about 2,800 characters of body). Enumerate with RSS: https://cdn.kids.donga.com/rss/gns_allArticle.xml (updated 2026-11-06; items link to /news/articleView.html?idxno=N). Section lists: /news/articleList.html?sc_section_code=.... Note: 어린이조선일보 (kid.chosun.com) also has static HTML, but its homepage articles date from February 2025 and look stale, so it is left out.

items.title: 구름빵
items.creator: 백희나 (Baek Heena)
items.why: A classic Korean picture book with a few short sentences per spread and clay-model photos that carry the story.
items.notes: 한솔수북, 2004. The English edition sold in Korea comes with QR-code audio.

items.title: 알사탕
items.creator: 백희나 (Baek Heena)
items.why: A short picture book in everyday spoken Korean (a dad's nagging, a dog's thoughts) by the Astrid Lindgren Award winner.
items.notes: Current Korean edition from Storybowl (2024); first published 2017 by 책읽는곰. English translation by Sophie Bowman (2021).

items.title: 달샤베트
items.creator: 백희나 (Baek Heena)
items.why: A very short summer-night picture book with simple repeated narration and diorama photos.
items.notes: English edition translated by Jieun Kiaer (Owlkids, 2021).

items.title: 장수탕 선녀님
items.creator: 백희나 (Baek Heena)
items.why: A funny picture book set in an old neighborhood bathhouse, with short dialogue and everyday cultural vocabulary.

items.title: 나는 개다
items.creator: 백희나 (Baek Heena)
items.why: First-person dog narrator in short simple sentences; a learner blog suggests it as a first Korean-only picture book.

items.title: 수박 수영장
items.creator: 안녕달 (Anyeongdal)
items.why: A bestselling summer picture book with very little text, mostly onomatopoeia and short lines.
items.notes: 창비, 2015. An English edition is mentioned by 90 Day Korean but no store link was verified.

items.title: 강아지똥
items.creator: 권정생 글, 정승각 그림 (Kwon Jeong-saeng)
items.why: Korea's best-known children's picture book; gentle narration and dialogue, longer text than a toddler book.
items.notes: 길벗어린이, 1996. No English print edition found (only the 2003 animated film); LTI lists the English title as 'Puppy Poo'.

items.title: 콩쥐팥쥐전 (다락원 한국어 학습문고)
items.titleEn: Darakwon Korean Readers: The Story of Kongjwi and Patjwi
items.creator: 김유미, 배세은 (Darakwon)
items.why: A graded reader that retells a classic Cinderella-type tale using beginner (초급) vocabulary and expressions; 80 pages.
items.notes: 8-volume series (토끼전, 콩쥐팥쥐전, 흥부전, 춘향전, 심청전, 홍길동전, 전우치전, 장화홍련전), levelled A1-C2 by the publisher. Aladin says 콩쥐팥쥐전 targets 초급 vocabulary.

items.title: Korean Stories for Language Learners
items.titleEn: Korean Stories for Language Learners: Traditional Folktales in Korean and English
items.creator: Julie Damron, EunSun You (Tuttle)
items.why: 42 folktales, each 1-3 pages, in simple Korean with English on the facing page, vocabulary lists and free audio; recommended for beginners.
items.notes: Stories get harder through the book; one reviewer says some passages are still hard for true beginners.

items.title: Korean Folktales for Language Learners
items.titleEn: Korean Folktales for Language Learners: Traditional Stories in English and Korean
items.creator: Sukyeon Cho, Yeon-Jeong Kim, Andrew Killick (Tuttle)
items.why: 36 folktales in parallel Korean and English with free audio, aimed at first- and second-year university students.
items.notes: Written by University of Sheffield Korean teachers; 2022.

items.title: 만복이네 떡집
items.creator: 김리리 (Kim Li-li)
items.why: A very popular first chapter book for Korean 1st-2nd graders ('난 책읽기가 좋아' series): large print, short chapters, illustrations.
items.notes: 비룡소, 2010. Long-running series (소원 떡집, 양순이네 떡집...). No official translation found. Level is a curator estimate from the series' target age.

items.title: 고양이 해결사 깜냥 1
items.creator: 홍민정 글, 김재희 그림
items.why: An illustrated early chapter-book series for lower primary grades, with lots of everyday apartment-life dialogue.
items.notes: 창비, 2020-; 9+ volumes. No official translation found. Level is a curator estimate.

items.title: 흥부전 (다락원 한국어 학습문고)
items.titleEn: Darakwon Korean Readers: The Story of Heungbu
items.creator: 김유미, 배세은 (Darakwon)
items.why: The third volume of Darakwon's graded series; retells Heungbu and Nolbu with intermediate (중급) core vocabulary.
items.notes: Same series also has 토끼전 (https://www.aladin.co.kr/shop/wproduct.aspx?ItemId=248007000) and 춘향전 (https://www.aladin.co.kr/shop/wproduct.aspx?ItemId=272795871).

items.title: 마당을 나온 암탉
items.titleEn: The Hen Who Dreamed She Could Fly
items.creator: 황선미 (Hwang Sun-mi)
items.why: A short children's novel (about 140 pages in English) with a simple fable plot; best-known modern Korean children's book and an animated film.

translations.title: The Hen Who Dreamed She Could Fly

items.notes: 사계절, 2000. Translated by Chi-Young Kim (Penguin, 2013). Ends with a death; can be sad for children.

items.title: 나쁜 어린이 표
items.creator: 황선미 (Hwang Sun-mi)
items.why: A long-time favorite primary-school story about a classroom sticker chart, in plain child-narrator Korean.
items.notes: 시공주니어 네버랜드 꾸러기 문고 64 (2024 edition). No official translation verified. Level is a curator estimate.

items.title: 긴긴밤
items.creator: 루리 (Ruri)
items.why: An illustrated award-winning upper-primary novel about a rhino and a penguin; short chapters, but emotionally deep.
items.notes: 문학동네 보름달문고 83, 2021; 제21회 문학동네어린이문학상 대상. No official English edition verified. Level is a curator estimate.

items.title: Short Stories in Korean for Intermediate Learners
items.titleEn: Short Stories in Korean for Intermediate Learners
items.creator: Olly Richards (Teach Yourself)
items.why: Eight stories written for low-mid intermediate learners (about B1), with glossaries and comprehension questions.

items.title: 아몬드
items.creator: 손원평 (Sohn Won-pyung)
items.why: A YA novel recommended for intermediate learners: short, plain sentences that match the narrator, who can't feel emotions.
items.notes: 창비, 2017 (also 다즐링 2023 edition). Some violence (a street attack, a school bully).

items.title: 위저드 베이커리
items.creator: 구병모 (Gu Byeong-mo)
items.why: A YA fantasy recommended as perfect for high-intermediate learners; vocabulary is harder than Almond.

translations.title: Les petits pains de la pleine lune

items.notes: 창비, 2009/2022. English edition 'The Wizard's Bakery' (tr. Jamie Chang, Wildfire/Headline, 2025). Includes child abuse themes.

items.title: 완득이
items.creator: 김려령 (Kim Ryeo-ryeong)
items.why: A funny first-person teen novel (about 200 pages) recommended by a learner blog for studying Korean; lots of colloquial speech.
items.notes: 창비 청소년문학상 winner, 2008; also a 2011 film. Slang and swearing from the teacher character.

items.title: 시간을 파는 상점
items.creator: 김선영 (Kim Seon-young)
items.why: A long-selling YA novel (100+ printings) with a high-school narrator and everyday school/family language.
items.notes: 자음과모음 청소년문학상, 2012. No official translation verified. Level is a curator estimate (YA = level 3-4).

items.title: 불편한 편의점
items.creator: 김호연 (Kim Ho-yeon)
items.why: Million-selling 'healing' novel told in short episodes at a Seoul convenience store, full of everyday dialogue.

translations.title: La asombrosa tienda de la señora Yeom

items.notes: 나무옆의자, 2021; sequel 불편한 편의점 2. English tr. Janet Hong (2025). The main character is a homeless man; some drinking. Level is a curator estimate; no learner source found.

items.title: 달러구트 꿈 백화점
items.creator: 이미예 (Lee Mi-ye)
items.why: A light fantasy bestseller made of short linked episodes in plain modern prose.
items.notes: 팩토리나인, 2020; volume 2 (2021) and prequel volume 0 (2026). English tr. Sandy Joosun Lee. Level is a curator estimate; no learner source found.

items.title: 어서 오세요, 휴남동 서점입니다
items.creator: 황보름 (Hwang Bo-reum)
items.why: A gentle slice-of-life novel in short chapters about a neighborhood bookshop; lots of conversation, little plot jargon.
items.notes: 클레이하우스, 2022. English tr. Shanna Tan (Bloomsbury, 2024). Characters talk about books and essays, so some reflective vocabulary. Level is a curator estimate.

items.title: 82년생 김지영
items.creator: 조남주 (Cho Nam-joo)
items.why: Short (about 170 pages) and written in flat, report-like narration, but it has statistics and social and workplace vocabulary.
items.notes: 민음사, 2016. 2019 film with Jung Yu-mi and Gong Yoo. Reviewers disagree about how easy it is; level is a curator estimate.

items.title: 채식주의자
items.creator: 한강 (Han Kang)
items.why: Nobel-winning literary prose with dense imagery and three narrators; for advanced readers.
items.notes: Mature: sexual content, violence, self-harm. English tr. Deborah Smith.

items.title: 소년이 온다
items.creator: 한강 (Han Kang)
items.why: Literary novel about the 1980 Gwangju Uprising, with second-person narration and historical vocabulary.
items.notes: Mature: graphic state violence and torture.

items.title: 엄마를 부탁해
items.creator: 신경숙 (Shin Kyung-sook)
items.why: A family drama told in four voices, including second person, with long literary sentences.
items.notes: 창비, 2008. Man Asian Literary Prize 2011. UK title 'Please Look After Mother'.

items.title: 펭귄 러브스 메브
items.creator: 펭귄 (Penguin)
items.why: Short autobiographical strips about a Korean-British couple's daily life, with simple everyday dialogue and pictures that carry the meaning.
items.notes: Completed (2010-2018). Some strips mix in English because one partner is British. Naver titleId comes from Korean Wikipedia's external link; comic.naver.com blocks automated fetching, so the Naver page itself was not opened.

items.title: 놓지마 정신줄
items.creator: 신태훈, 나승훈
items.why: Gag comedy about a family's everyday life: each episode is a short self-contained joke told in casual spoken Korean.
items.notes: Very long (1,000+ episodes over several seasons); readers can dip in anywhere. Some wordplay. No official translation found. Level is judged from genre and format (no learner review found). Naver titleIds come from Korean Wikipedia, not opened directly.

items.title: 와라! 편의점
items.creator: 지강민 (Ji Kang-min)
items.why: Short self-contained gags about a part-timer at a convenience store, built on everyday shop vocabulary and simple exchanges with customers.
items.notes: Started 2008, episodic. Has an anime adaptation. No official translation found on WEBTOON. Level is judged from format (no learner review found). Naver titleId comes from English Wikipedia, not opened directly.

items.title: 혈액형에 관한 간단한 고찰
items.titleEn: A Simple Thinking About Blood Type
items.creator: 박동선 (Park Dong-sun)
items.why: Four-panel gag strips, so each joke is only a few short lines; the same personality vocabulary comes back again and again.
items.notes: The humour is built on blood-type personality stereotypes. Has a Japanese anime adaptation and print books. Level is judged from format (no learner review found). Naver titleId comes from English Wikipedia, not opened directly.

items.title: 어쿠스틱 라이프
items.creator: 난다 (Nanda)
items.why: Diary comic about a married couple and later their toddler: short episodes of everyday home conversation, with the art carrying a lot of the meaning.
items.notes: Long-running (290+ episodes). Kakao lists the genre as comic/everyday life. No official translation found. Level is judged from genre (no learner review found).

items.title: 연의 편지
items.creator: 조현아 (Hyeon A Cho)
items.why: Only 12 chapters: a gentle school story about a girl following letters left by a former student, told in plain, child-friendly Korean.
items.notes: Completed 2018 (12 chapters). The English print edition made the ALA's 2025 Great Graphic Novels for Teens top ten, and an animated film came out in 2025. Level is judged from length and audience. Naver titleId comes from English Wikipedia, not opened directly.

items.title: 오늘도 형제는 평화롭다
items.creator: GIMS
items.why: Short completed comedy (50 episodes) about two close brothers at home: casual sibling banter about everyday situations.
items.notes: Completed 2017 and adapted into a web drama. No official English title or translation found. Level is judged from genre and length only. Naver titleId comes from Korean Wikipedia, not opened directly.

items.title: 마음의 소리
items.creator: 조석 (Jo Seok)
items.why: Short stand-alone gag episodes about the author's family; the sentences are short, but the slang and puns make it harder than it looks.
items.notes: Completed 2020 after 1,200+ episodes. Learner blogs call it beginner-friendly but warn about slang and cultural in-jokes, so it is placed at 3. Naver titleId comes from Korean Wikipedia, not opened directly.

items.title: 유미의 세포들
items.creator: 이동건 (Lee Dong-geon)
items.why: Everyday office and dating life of a woman in her 30s, with clear visual gags; the 'cell' personifications add some biology words.

translations.title: ยูมิกับเซลล์สมองสุดอลเวง [Yumi's Cells]

items.notes: Completed 2020 (512 episodes) and adapted as a TV drama. The English WEBTOON page currently lists only about 33 episodes, and the French page is season 3 only. Learner ratings vary: Natively forum TOPIK 3, but Natively rates print vol. 12 at ~TOPIK 4, and Lingopie says it is challenging at first. Naver titleId comes from English Wikipedia, not opened directly.

items.title: 여신강림
items.creator: 야옹이 (Yaongyi)
items.why: High-school romance with mostly everyday teen dialogue (school, friends, makeup), so the vocabulary is predictable and practical.

translations.title: ความลับของนางฟ้า [True Beauty]

items.notes: Completed 2023 and adapted as a TV drama. Has the widest set of official translations in this list. Naver titleId comes from English Wikipedia, not opened directly.

items.title: 연애혁명
items.why: High-school romantic comedy driven by casual classroom banter: a lot of everyday spoken Korean with some teen slang.
items.notes: Completed 2023 (434 episodes over 3 seasons). No English WEBTOON edition found. Level is judged from genre. Naver titleId comes from Korean Wikipedia, not opened directly.

items.title: 내 아이디는 강남미인
items.creator: 기맹기 (Gi Maeng-gi)
items.why: University campus story with natural student conversation; about 90 episodes, so it can be finished.
items.notes: Completed 2017 (90 episodes plus a 4-episode side story). Deals with plastic surgery and lookism. Adapted as a TV drama. Level is judged from genre. Naver titleId comes from English Wikipedia, not opened directly.

items.title: 좀비딸
items.creator: 이윤창 (Lee Yun-chang)
items.why: Family comedy (a father hiding his zombie daughter at home); dialogue is mostly short, warm, everyday family talk.

translations.title: My Daughter is a Zombie - Kisah Asli Film

items.notes: Completed 2020. The English WEBTOON page currently lists 11 episodes. Mild zombie comedy; not gory. Has an EBS animation and a film. Level is judged from genre. Naver titleId comes from English Wikipedia, not opened directly.

items.title: 맘마미안
items.creator: MiTi, GUGU
items.why: Family drama (a daughter thrown back into her mother's youth) with everyday home and school conversation.
items.notes: Completed 2021. The English WEBTOON page currently lists only 7 episodes. Has a Chinese donghua adaptation. Level is judged from genre. Naver titleId comes from English Wikipedia, not opened directly.

items.title: 청춘 블라썸
items.creator: 홍덕 (Hongduck), 네모네 (Nemone)
items.why: Linked high-school stories with natural teen dialogue about friends, crushes and worries.
items.notes: Completed 2023. The English WEBTOON page currently lists only 9 episodes. Touches on teen issues such as bullying and loss. Level is judged from genre. Naver titleId comes from English Wikipedia, not opened directly.

items.title: 가우스전자
items.creator: 곽백수 (Gwak Baek-su)
items.why: Short office gags at an electronics company: good for workplace vocabulary and polite company speech, one joke per episode.
items.notes: Completed 2019 (1,500+ episodes). No official translation found on WEBTOON. Adapted as a TV drama. Level is judged from genre. Naver titleIds come from Korean Wikipedia, not opened directly.

items.title: 나빌레라
items.creator: HUN, 지민 (Jimmy)
items.why: Quiet, warm story of a retired man learning ballet: slow pacing, short exchanges and lots of panels without text.
items.notes: Completed. Older characters use some polite and dialect-tinged speech. Adapted as a Netflix drama. Level is judged from style.

items.title: 김 비서가 왜 그럴까
items.creator: 김명미, 정경윤 (original novel)
items.why: Office romantic comedy with clear formal-vs-casual speech contrasts (boss and secretary), mostly dialogue-driven scenes.
items.notes: Completed. Adapted from the web novel of the same name (see its own entry) and adapted as a TV drama. KakaoPage URL verified from search results (KakaoPage pages render client-side).

items.title: 외모지상주의
items.creator: 박태준 (Park Tae-jun)
items.why: School setting with lots of everyday speech, but heavy slang, insults and fight scenes push it past the beginner stage.
items.notes: MATURE THEMES: violence, bullying, gangs; later arcs include sexual violence and stalking. Ongoing (600+ episodes, weekly). Level is judged from style. Naver titleId comes from English Wikipedia, not opened directly.

items.title: 치즈인더트랩
items.creator: 순끼 (Soonkki)
items.why: Realistic university life, but the drama runs on subtext, inner monologue and long conversations.

translations.title: チーズ・イン・ザ・トラップ

items.notes: Completed 2017. Psychological tension and some stalking/violence. Adapted as a TV drama and a film. Level is judged from style. Naver titleId comes from English Wikipedia, not opened directly.

items.title: 이태원 클라쓰
items.creator: 광진 (Kwang Jin)
items.why: Adult drama about running a pub: everyday speech, plus business vocabulary and some rough language.
items.notes: Completed (Tapas lists 81 episodes). Some violence, drinking and prison scenes. Piccoma (ja) carries a localized edition, 六本木クラス, but no reading-page URL could be verified. Adapted as a hit TV drama.

items.title: 나 혼자만 레벨업
items.creator: 장성락 (DUBU, REDICE STUDIO), 현군, 추공 (original)
items.why: Action-heavy panels with short battle lines and game-style status windows that repeat; the fantasy terms come back again and again.
items.notes: MATURE: graphic violence. Completed (179 episodes plus a 21-episode side story). Also available in Japanese on Piccoma (俺だけレベルアップな件; only feature/promo pages could be verified, not a product page) and in English print from Yen Press. KakaoPage content ID taken from verified episode URLs in search results. Level is judged from style.

items.title: 여중생A
items.creator: 허5파6 (Heo5pa6)
items.why: Told through a lonely middle-schooler's inner voice: simple words, but long narration and emotional subtext.
items.notes: MATURE THEMES: domestic violence, bullying, school violence, online harassment. Completed 2017 (124 episodes). The English title is descriptive (no official translation found). Adapted as a film. Level is judged from style. Naver titleId comes from Korean Wikipedia, not opened directly.

items.title: 집이 없어
items.creator: 와난 (Wanan)
items.why: Slice-of-life drama about homeless teenagers sharing a house: everyday speech, but long emotional conversations.
items.notes: MATURE THEMES: abuse, bullying, a stabbing, trauma. Completed 2024 (269 chapters). No English WEBTOON edition found. Level is judged from style. Naver titleId comes from English Wikipedia, not opened directly.

items.title: 미생
items.creator: 윤태호 (Yoon Tae-ho)
items.why: Realistic trading-company drama full of business jargon, formal office speech and baduk (Go) metaphors.
items.notes: Part 2 ongoing or irregular. The Piccoma link is the official promo page for the Japanese edition (exclusive on Piccoma since 2016), not the reading page. No English digital edition found on Tapas. Adapted as the TV drama 'Misaeng'. Level is judged from style.

items.title: 신의 탑
items.creator: SIU (이종휘)
items.why: Dense fantasy world-building with invented terms, long explanations and a huge cast.
items.notes: Ongoing since 2010 (650+ episodes; currently on a break after the season 3 finale). Violence. Level is judged from genre. Naver titleId comes from English Wikipedia, not opened directly.

items.title: 전지적 독자 시점
items.creator: Sleepy-C, UMI, 싱숑 (original)
items.why: Apocalyptic fantasy with system messages, invented terms and literary narration taken from the novel.

translations.title: Omniscient Reader อ่านชะตาวันสิ้นโลก
全知的な読者の視点から

items.notes: MATURE: graphic violence and gore. Ongoing (300+ episodes, currently on a break). Adapted as a 2025 film. Level is judged from genre. Naver titleId comes from English Wikipedia, not opened directly.

items.title: 화산귀환
items.creator: LICO, ARCHE, 비가 (original)
items.why: Murim (martial-arts) setting full of Sino-Korean sect and martial-arts vocabulary and old-fashioned speech styles.
items.notes: Ongoing (weekly). Martial-arts violence. Level is judged from genre. Naver titleId comes from English Wikipedia, not opened directly.

items.title: 김비서가 왜 그럴까
items.creator: 정경윤 (Jeong Gyeong-yun)
items.why: Contemporary office rom-com with lots of dialogue, modern everyday settings and an official English translation to check against.
items.notes: Completed. Tapas English: 73 episodes, chapter 1 readable, more free episodes after login. KakaoPage usually offers wait-for-free episodes, but this could not be confirmed per title. Level is judged from genre: contemporary romance web novels use simple, repetitive language (Natively forum).

items.title: 사내 맞선
items.creator: 해화 (Haehwa)
items.why: Office rom-com (a fake blind date with the CEO) with short scenes and lots of modern, everyday dialogue.
items.notes: Completed (69 main episodes plus side stories). Tapas English: 112 episodes, free episodes after login. The webtoon adaptation is on Tapas (https://tapas.io/series/a-business-proposal), and the story was adapted as a hit TV drama. Learners suggest stories you already know from a drama as an easier start.

items.title: 진심이 닿다
items.creator: 예거 (Jäger)
items.why: Contemporary rom-com set at a law firm: modern dialogue-driven scenes, with some legal words.
items.notes: Completed (100+ episodes). A webtoon version is also on KakaoPage (https://page.kakao.com/content/52311048), and the story became a tvN drama. No official translation found. Level is judged from genre.

items.title: 나 혼자만 레벨업
items.creator: 추공 (Chugong)
items.why: Fast, plain action prose with repeated game-system phrases, and there is an official English edition to compare against.
items.notes: Completed. Violence. Yen Press published 8 English volumes (2021-2023). Piccoma (ja) runs a novel edition (prologue to chapter 100 were free in one campaign), but no product URL could be verified. Level is judged from style.

items.title: 템빨
items.creator: 박새날 (Park Saenal)
items.why: VR-game fantasy with lots of repeated game vocabulary and comic inner monologue; very long, so the words recur.
items.notes: Completed and very long. Wuxiaworld gives one free chapter about every 23 hours. The webtoon adaptation is on Tapas (https://tapas.io/series/overgeared). Level is judged from genre.

items.title: 데뷔 못 하면 죽는 병 걸림
items.creator: 백덕수 (Baek Deok-su)
items.why: K-pop idol survival story told through casual, funny inner monologue and modern slang that K-pop fans will recognise.
items.notes: Long (Tapas English has 567 episodes). Heavy on internet and fandom slang. The webtoon version is on KakaoPage (https://page.kakao.com/content/59782511). Level is judged from style.

items.title: 괴담에 떨어져도 출근을 해야 하는구나
items.titleEn: Got Dropped Into a Ghost Story, Still Gotta Work
items.creator: 백덕수 (Baek Deok-su)
items.why: Office-worker horror comedy: modern workplace speech and memo-style rule lists that repeat.
items.notes: MATURE: horror, violence and gore (KakaoPage shows a content warning on episode 1). KakaoPage ID taken from verified episode URLs in search results. A webtoon version exists. No official English translation found on Tapas. Level is judged from style.

items.title: SSS급 죽어야 사는 헌터
items.creator: 신노아 (Sinnoa)
items.why: Hunter/tower fantasy with plain action prose and recurring skill and system terms.
items.notes: Munpia lists it as paid (400 posts). Wuxiaworld gives one free chapter every 23 hours. Violence. The webtoon is on KakaoPage and on Tapas in English. Level is judged from genre.

items.title: 그녀가 공작저로 가야 했던 사정
items.titleEn: The Reason Why Raeliana Ended up at the Duke's Mansion
items.creator: 밀차 (Milcha)
items.why: Romance fantasy driven by witty dialogue; noble titles and formal speech add difficulty, but the romance plot keeps it easy to follow.

translations.title: The Reason Why Raeliana Ended up at the Duke's Mansion

items.notes: Completed (9 book volumes including side stories). Tappytoon English: episodes 1-4 free. The webtoon is on KakaoPage (https://page.kakao.com/content/50242834). Level is judged from genre.

items.title: 전지적 독자 시점
items.creator: 싱숑 (singNsong)
items.why: Literary, self-referential prose with invented terms, quotations and long narration.
items.notes: Munpia lists it as paid (1,000+ posts including the sequel). Graphic violence. Also published in Thai (Levon) and Chinese print editions, per Wikipedia (no URLs verified). Level is judged from style.

items.title: 화산귀환
items.titleEn: Return of the Mount Hua Sect
items.creator: 비가 (Biga)
items.why: Murim novel full of Sino-Korean martial-arts vocabulary and archaic speech, though the comic tone helps.
items.notes: Ongoing and long. Wikipedia says Webnovel licensed an English translation as 'Return of the Mount Hua Sect', but webnovel.com blocked verification, so that link is left out. Naver Series link comes from English Wikipedia; Naver blocks automated fetching. Webtoon: see its own entry. Level is judged from genre.

items.title: 재혼 황후
items.creator: 알파타르트 (Alphatart)
items.why: Court romance with formal imperial speech, honorifics and political vocabulary.

translations.title: 再婚承認を要求します

items.notes: The English novel was published by Yonder (no link verified). The translations listed are of the webtoon adaptation (Naver Webtoon titleId 735661 per Wikipedia). Adapted as a Disney+ series (Nov 2026). Naver link comes from English Wikipedia, not opened directly. Level is judged from genre.

items.title: 악역의 엔딩은 죽음뿐
items.creator: 권겨을 (Gwon Gyeoeul)
items.why: Otome-game-world romance fantasy with noble formal speech and a lot of inner monologue.

translations.title: Villains Are Destined to Die (novel), Vol. 1

items.notes: Some violence and dark themes (abuse within the family). The webtoon is on KakaoPage (https://page.kakao.com/content/54845189). Level is judged from genre.

items.title: 구르미 그린 달빛
items.creator: 윤이수 (Yoon Yi-soo)
items.why: Joseon-era romance with historical court vocabulary and archaic speech forms.
items.notes: Completed (serialized 2013, 5-volume print edition 2015). Wikipedia notes a Mandarin translation; no official English translation found. Adapted as the drama 'Love in the Moonlight'. Naver Series link comes from English Wikipedia; Naver blocks automated fetching. Level is judged from genre.

items.title: 귀환자의 마법은 특별해야 합니다
items.titleEn: A Returner's Magic Should Be Special
items.creator: 유소난 (Usonan)
items.why: Magic-academy fantasy with dense spell and system vocabulary and long expository passages.
items.notes: Completed. No official English translation of the novel found; the webtoon (KakaoPage https://page.kakao.com/content/51185123) is published in English by Tappytoon and Yen Press. Level is judged from genre.

items.title: Learn to Read Korean in 15 Minutes
items.titleEn: Learn to Read Korean in 15 Minutes
items.creator: Ryan Estrada
items.why: A single illustrated comic that teaches every basic Hangul letter with picture mnemonics; the fastest possible first contact.
items.notes: step 1: Hangul (first 15 minutes). Free to read on the web, no login. English only. Mnemonic shortcut only: follow with htsk-unit-0 for pronunciation and syllable blocks.

items.title: How to Study Korean - Unit 0: Learning How to Read
items.titleEn: How to Study Korean - Unit 0: Learning How to Read
items.creator: HowtoStudyKorean.com
items.why: Three lessons that build Hangul letter by letter into syllable blocks, with clickable audio for every letter and table plus dictation/reading-practice videos.
items.notes: step 1: Hangul (main lesson). Site states lessons will always be free (app, PDFs, store are paid extras). Lesson 1 is offered in Italian, German, Spanish, Russian, French, Portuguese, Dutch, Polish, Greek, Bulgarian, Romanian, Azerbaijani, Turkish, Ukrainian, Persian, Kurdish and Arabic (volunteer translations on the same site; links not individually verified).

items.title: Hangul - Free Complete Guide (Lingrow)
items.creator: Lingrow
items.why: Interactive Hangul chart: tap any letter to hear it and see romanization plus an example word; includes syllable blocks, pronunciation rules and a 7-day practice plan.
items.notes: step 1: Hangul (reference chart to keep open while practising). Page says guide and chart are completely free; it is marketing for the Lingrow app (paid features: pronunciation scoring, SRS). Updated Oct 2026. English only.

items.title: GO! Billy Korean
items.titleEn: Learn Korean with GO! Billy Korean
items.creator: Billy Go
items.why: Clear English-language video lessons starting from the Hangul alphabet and first grammar, popular with total beginners.
items.notes: step 1-2: watch the Hangul videos alongside htsk-unit-0, then beginner grammar videos. Free on YouTube; explanations in English.

items.title: How to Study Korean - Unit 1
items.creator: HowtoStudyKorean.com
items.why: 25 free text lessons (20-30 words each, audio for every word and sentence) covering sentence structure, conjugation, numbers, time, questions and first connectors like ~고 싶다.
items.notes: step 2: first grammar. Free lessons; optional paid workbook PDF, app, Anki decks. Free YouTube sentence/dictation practice playlists linked. Dense and grammar-heavy - pair with a video channel. Same volunteer translations as Unit 0 for many lessons.

items.title: First Step Korean
items.creator: Yonsei University (Seung Hae Kang) on Coursera
items.why: Short university video course from zero: Hangeul, greetings and introductions, family, time and dates, daily life - a gentle structured first month.
items.notes: step 2: structured beginner course (can also replace step 1). Taught in English; Coursera lists subtitles in 23 languages (not enumerated on the page). Free audit widely reported by learners and review sites, but the course page itself only mentions paid certificate / free trial - curator should confirm audit option before labelling 'free'. ~4.9 stars from ~53k ratings.

items.title: Talk To Me In Korean
items.creator: Talk To Me In Korean (TTMIK)
items.why: Large free library of short lessons on everyday expressions and grammar from the best-known Korean-learning publisher.
items.notes: step 2+: free companion to any course. Mostly English explanations.

items.title: 온라인 세종학당 (Online King Sejong Institute)
items.creator: King Sejong Institute Foundation (Korean government, MCST)
items.why: The Korean government's official online course: level test, then self-learning or tutor-assisted (Cyber Korean) courses in 5- and 10-week terms using the Sejong Korean textbooks.
items.notes: step 3: official structured course. Free with registration, but courses open in enrolment windows (register, take level test, then apply each term). Course language filter on the LMS shows Korean and English; third-party sources mention more languages (Russian, Vietnamese, Spanish, French, Chinese) - unverified.

items.title: 누리세종학당
items.creator: King Sejong Institute Foundation
items.why: Official portal with a Korean Study Roadmap, a Hangul character introduction, the official Sejong Korean textbooks as free e-books, learning materials, practice and a level test.
items.notes: step 3: textbooks (Sejong Korean 1A/1B etc.) to accompany the Online KSI course. Free member registration required; e-books are read online only (no PDF download/printing), interface reported as finicky. Site menu available in English and Korean.

items.title: 세종한국어 앱
items.creator: King Sejong Institute Foundation
items.why: Official KSI app with vocabulary, grammar, conversation and travel sections plus an AI teacher, from beginner level up.
items.notes: step 3: vocab/grammar drilling alongside the Sejong textbooks. Reported free of charge (app store listings, KSIF); the app info page itself does not state the price. Interface languages not confirmed (English; Spanish versions of older apps reported).

items.title: Duolingo Korean
items.creator: Duolingo
items.why: Bite-size gamified lessons that start with Hangul; good as a daily habit next to a real course.
items.notes: any step: daily habit. Free app and web (Super/Max subscription optional). The verified link is the course for English speakers; Duolingo also offers Korean from some other base languages (check the app's course list). Thin on grammar explanations.

items.title: LingoDeer
items.creator: LingoDeer
items.why: App designed for Asian languages: Hangul unit then grammar-explained lessons; stronger grammar notes than Duolingo.
items.notes: any step: alternative to Duolingo. Freemium (first units free per learner reports; full access is a subscription - site shows only promo pricing). Site language menu: English, German, Spanish, French, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Thai, Turkish, Vietnamese, Traditional Chinese, Arabic (which base languages the Korean course supports is not confirmed).

items.title: Talk To Me In Korean - Courses
items.titleEn: Talk To Me In Korean - Core Grammar curriculum
items.creator: Talk To Me In Korean (TTMIK)
items.why: The classic Level 1 path (starts with Hangeul, then Core Grammar) used by huge numbers of learners; one full lesson free to try.
items.notes: upgrade path after free resources. Only one free lesson (Core Grammar 1, email signup); the 1,700+ lesson library is a subscription (from about $7/month billed annually; 7-day trial on Standard plan). Free level test at https://courses.talktomeinkorean.com/level-test (linked from the page). talktomeinkorean.com redirects here. English only.

items.title: 한국어교수학습샘터
items.titleEn: Center for Teaching and Learning Korean (NIKL)
items.creator: National Institute of Korean Language (국립국어원)
items.why: NIKL's official download centre of Korean textbooks and materials grouped by learner type (adults, immigrants, overseas learners, children).
items.notes: optional / for curators and tutors: interface Korean only and aimed mainly at teachers; free/licensing terms vary per item (see the site's copyright policy). kcenter.korean.go.kr redirects here. Low priority for absolute beginners.
